  HTTPS://YOUTUBE.COM/@SOUTHGATECA90280

VICE MAYOR, Joshua Barron  CITY TREASURER, Jose De La Paz

If you would like to participate in this meeting, you can participate via the following
options:

1. VIEW THE MEETING LIVE ONLINE AT: https://youtube.com/@SouthGateCA90280
Please allow up to 24 hours after the meeting for the archive to be available.
2. PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING by emailing the City Clerk at:
yglaze@sogate.org no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please write
"Public Comment" in the subject line.
3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON
*The disruption in service of any alternative method does not prelude the City Council
or other legislative
body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Comments From The Audience - Non-Agenda Items
During this time, members of the public may address the City Council regarding any items not
listed on the agenda and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council and not on
this agenda. Comments from the audience will be limited to three (3) minutes per speaker;
unless authorized by the Mayor, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another
member's time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless
authorized by law. The collective initial period of time for comments from the audience shall
be limited to 45 minutes. Any speaker that did not get a chance to speak during this segment
due to the 45-minute limitations will be able to speak at the end of the meeting prior to
adjournment.

  3
 Note: The City Council desires to provide all members of the public with the opportunity to
address the Council. Nevertheless, obscene language, comments intended to
disrupt/interfere, other actions which disrupt the progress of the meeting or slanderous
comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or may constitute a violation of
South Gate Municipal Code Section1.04.110.

Reports And Comments From City Officials

During this time, members of the City Council will report on matters pertaining to their service
on various intergovernmental boards and commissions as a representative of the City
pursuant to Assembly Bill 1234. City Council Members will also have an opportunity to
comment on matters not on the agenda.

Consent Calendar Items

Agenda Items 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and 11 are Consent Calendar Items. All items including
Ordinances, Resolutions and Contracts, may be approved by adoption of the Consent
Calendar, individually and collectively by one (1) motion. There will be no separate discussion
of these items unless Members of the City Council, the public, or staff request that specific
items be removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion and action. Members
of the public are permitted to speak on any item listed but their time period is limited to three
(3) minutes in total.

Any motion to introduce or adopt an Ordinance on the Consent Calendar shall be: (1) a
motion to waive the reading of the Ordinance and introduce the Ordinance or (2) a motion to
waive the reading of the Ordinance and adopt the Ordinance, as appropriate.

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

  8
 The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City

  9
 Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

ANALYSIS:

Appeal  filed  against  the Planning  Commission's  Decision

The appeal  filed  by the appellant  (Attachment  C) challenges  the Planning  Commission's  March
18, 2025, approval  of Vesting  Tentative  Tract Map (TTM)  No. 84531  and the corresponding  Class
32 CEQA  Categorical  Exemption.  The  appeal  asserts  that the project  does not satisfy  all five
criteria  for  the exemption  and is subject  to the "unusual  circumstances"  exception  due to its
proximity  to a high  school,  unresolved  traffic  safety  issues, and a history  of site contamination.

Staff has reviewed  the appeal in detail,  including  the accompanying  legal memorandum,  and offers
the following  responses  to each primary  area of concern:

1.  Traffic  and Pedestrian  Safety  Near  Legacy  High  School

  Appeal  Concern:  The project  site is adjacent  to Legacy  High  School,  and the appeal  argues
  that  this  proximity  creates  unique  and unresolved  traffic  and pedestrian  safety  issues.  The
  replacement  of  a concrete  K-rail  with  an emergency  access  gate,  and the  deferral  of  a
  comprehensive  traffic  study under  Condition  No. 60, are cited as improper  under  CEQA  case
  law.

  Staff Response:  A preliminary  traffic  evaluation,  including  a Vehicle  Miles  Traveled  (VMT)
  analysis  consistent  with  CEQA  Guidelines,  determined  that the project  falls below  established
  thresholds  for  significant  traffic  impacts.  Therefore,  the  project  qualifies  for  a CEQA
  Categorical  Exemption  (Class  32 - Infill  development).

  Condition  No. 60, imposed  by the Planning  Commission,  is independent  of CEQA  and is not
  intended  as mitigation  for any CEQA-identified  impact.  Rather,  it will  serve to evaluate  fiiture
  improvements  that could  enhance  emergency  vehicle  access and facilitate  City  maintenance
  operations  in the project  vicinity.

  Adella  Avenue  will  continue  to remain  closed  to regular  vehicular  traffic.  As part of the City's
  broader  circulation  planning  and  public  safety  efforts,  Condition  No.  60  requires  the
  replacement  of the existing  K-rail  barrier  with  a decorative-style  barrier.  This new barrier  will
  maintain  the current  traffic  restrictions  while  providing  controlled  access for emergency  and
  maintenance  vehicles.  The barrier's  final  design  and functionality  will  be determined  through
  the City's  standard  review  process.

  To support  this effort,  staff has worked  with  the project  proponent  to revise  Condition  No. 60
  to  clarify  both  the  City's  intent  to  maintain  the  existing  street  closure  and the  funding
  mechanism  for future  public  improvements.  However,  the revised  condition  was not accepted,
  and it remains  in its original  form.

2.  Air  Quality  and Noise  Impacts

  Appeal  Concern:  The appeal raises the issue of cumulative  air quality  impacts,  especially  near
  a school  and residential  area already  burdened  by freeway  traffic  and argues for a fiill  Health

  23
   Risk  Assessment.  Noise  impacts,  particularly  during  construction,  are  also  flagged  as a
  concern.

  Staff Response:  Air quality  and noise assessments  were prepared  in accordance  with  applicable
  professional  standards  and regional  environmental  guidelines  and concluded  that the project's
  anticipated  construction  and operational  emissions,  as well  as projected  noise  levels,  will  not
  exceed  recognized  significance  thresholds.  Although  the project  is categorically  exempt  from
  CEQA  and not subject  to formal  mitigation  requirements,  standard  conditions  of approval  and
  best  management  practices  will  help  minimize  temporary  construction  impacts,  such  as
  requirements  for dust control  and restricted  work  hours.  There  is no substantial  evidence  in the
  record  indicating  that the project  would  result  in significant  impacts  related  to air quality  or
  nOlSe.

3.  Soil Contamination  and Site Safety

  Appeal  Concern:  The  appeal  references  the site's  industrial  history  and alleges  insufficient
  analysis  of soil contamination  and vapor  intrusion  risks.  It argues that CEQA  requires  a Phase
  II Environmental  Site  Assessment  and full  disclosure  of hazardous  materials  risks  before
  project  approval.

  Staff  Response:  The site has undergone  appropriate  environmental  review  and remediation,
  and correspondence  from  the Los  Angeles  County  Fire  Department's  Hazardous  Materials
  Division  confirms  that the site has been adequately  cleaned.  This  oversight  ensures  that the
  project  does not pose a significant  risk related  to hazardous  materials.

  Furthermore,  the project  site is not listed  on the Cortese  List,  which  would  otherwise  trigger
  additional  CEQA  requirements.  However,  the applicant  remains  subject  to the oversight  of all
  applicable  outside  regulatory  agencies.  Any  future  work  at the site must  continue  to comply
  with  strict  requirements  and standards  established  by those  agencies,  including  monitoring,
  reporting,  and  response  protocols  related  to  contamination.  Based  on  the  documented
  regulatory  oversight,  there is no substantial  evidence  in the record  indicating  the presence  of
  environmental  conditions  that would  preclude  the use of a Class 32 categorical  exemption.

4.  Unusual  Circumstances  and CEQA  Exceptions

  Appeal  Concern:  The  appellant  invokes  CEQA  Guidelines  §15300.2(c),  claiming  that  the
  combination  of school  adjacency,  deferred  traffic  analysis,  and soil contamination  constitutes
  "unusual  circumstances"  requiring  disqualification  from  the Class 32 exemption.

  Staff Response:  The Class 32 exemption  applies  to infill  projects  in urbanized  areas that meet
  five specific  criteria,  all of which  this project  satisfies.  The "unusual  circumstances"  exception
  applies  only  if a fair argument  can be made,  supported  by substantial  evidence  that a specific
  impact  would  result  from  the project's  unique  features.

  In this case, there is no substantial  evidence  in the record  demonstrating  that these conditions
  rise to the level  of a reasonably  foreseeable  significant  impact.  Although  the project  is near a
  school  and on a formerly  industrial  site,  these  factors  are not  uncommon  in urban  infill
  development  and  are mitigated  through  standard  regulatory  procedures.  The  existence  of
  community  concern  does  not  itself  meet  the  legal  threshold  for  triggering  this  CEQA
  exception.

  24
 CONCLUSION:

All  applicable  procedures  in  reviewing  and  approving  Vesting  TTM  No.  84531  have  been
followed,  including  a thorough  analysis  of  environmental  factors  consistent  with  CEQA
requirements.  The  appeal  does  not  present  substantial  evidence  of  significant  environmental
impacts  or "unusual  circumstances"  that  would  invalidate  the use of the Class  32 categorical
exemption.

As such, staff recomtnends  that the City  Council  uphold  the Planning  Commission's  approval  and
affirm  the CEQA  exemption  for the project  by adopting  a Resolution.  Alternatively,  City  Council
could  consider  upholding  the Plaru'iing  Commission's  approval  with  a revised  condition  clarifying
that Adella  Avenue  will  remain  closed  to regular  vehicular  traffic  and establishes  the applicant's

SUBJECT:  Tentative  Tract  Map No. 84531

PROJECT  PROPOSAL/REQUEST
Consideration  of a Vesting  Tentative  Tract  Map  (TTM)  to allow  the subdivision  of one parcel  into a 54-
unit residential  condominium  development  located  at 10130  Adella  Avenue,  within  the Industrial  Flex (IF)
zone in the Tweedy  Boulevard  Specific  Plan.

PROJECT  OVERVIEW

*  General  Plan Designation:  Industrial
*  ,:  Tweedy  Boulevard  Specific  Plan (TBSP);  Industrial  Flex (IF)
*  Project  Location:  10130  Adella  Avenue
*  Assessor's  Parcel Number:  6221-026-020

*  :  Nick  Patterson  (City  Ventures),  on behalf  of South Gate I Inv, LLC

BACKGROUND
Site Characteristics:  The subject  property  is a vacant  lot measuring  approximately  2.02 acres, located  at the
intersection  of Adella  Avenue  and Legacy  Lane,  within  the Tweedy  Boulevard  Specific  Plan  area. The
subject  site is a relatively  flat, rectangular  shaped undeveloped  propeity,  and primarily  comprised  of ruderal
vegetation  and coarse fill.  Fencing  currently  surrounds  the subject  site.

Surroundings:  The site is surrounded  by a mix of residential,  commercial,  and institutional  uses, with Adella
Avenue  and Legacy  Lane  providing  primary  access. Legacy  High  School  and the Legacy  High  School
Softball  Fields  are located  directly  north  of the subject  property,  across the street from  Legacy  Lane. There
is an adjoining  light  industrial/commercial-truck  yard  directly  east of the subject  property,  and the Los
Angeles  River  and 710 Freeway  further  east. Directly  south  of the subject  property,  there  is a Southern
California  Edison  (SCE)  utility  easement  with  overhead  power  lines in place,  and single-family  residential
uses are located  south  of the SCE  easement,  within  the TBSP.  Immediately  west  of the Project  site are
Legacy  Lane and Adella  Avenue.  North  of Legacy  Lane and west of Adella  Avenue  are undeveloped  lots
within  the Legacy  High  School  Complex.  South  of Legacy  Lane  and west of Adella  Avenue  are single-
family  residential  uses.

Proposed  Vesting  TTM  and Associated  Development:  The applicant  is requesting  approval  of a Vesting
TTM  (Attachment  B) to allow  the subdivision  of one parcel  (2.02  acres)  into  54 condominium  units  in
connection  with  a proposed  residential  development  located  at 10130  Adella  Avenue.

The proposed  development  involves  the construction  of 54 new residential  condominium  units (for sale),
comprising  three-story  attached  townhomes  in six buildings.  Each building  would  contain  nine dwelling
units and have a maximum  height  of approximately  3 7 feet. The units would  consist  of a mix  of floor  plans

with  three-to  four-bedroom  options,  ranging  in size from  1,304 to 1,705  square feet. Six (12 percent)  of the
units would  be provided  at the moderate-income  level.

Administrative  Plan Review  & Design  Review:  The proposed  (54-unit  townhome)  development  project
associated  with  the requested  Vesting  TTM  is deemed  a "Multifamily  Residential"  use in accordance  with
the provisions  of the Zoning  Code. "Multifamily  Residential"  uses are permitted  by-right  with the approval
of an Administrative  Plan Review.  In addition,  Design  Review  is required  for the proposed  development
since  it involves  a parcel  measuring  greater  than  15,000  square  feet.  Administrative  Plan  Review  and
Design  Review  are discretionary  procedures  conducted  by staff.  Therefore,  the  overall  design  of the
proposed  development  is not subject  to review  by the Planning  Commission.  The Planning  Commission
may  only  take action  on the TTM  as it relates  to tlie proposed  subdivision  of a parcel  for condominium
purposes  to accommodate  the proposed  development.

ANALYSIS:
Municipal  Code  Requirements  for  Vesting  TTM  Approval:  Pursuant  to South  Gate  Municipal  Code
(SGMC)  Section  12.10.060,  the TTM  shall be heard by the Plai'u'iing  Commission  at a scheduled  hearing;
and action  shall be taken to approve,  conditionally  approve,  or disapprove  such TTM.  Subsequently,  a Final
Map  shall  be prepared  and forwarded  to the City  Council  for final  review,  in which  they  shall  approve,
deny, or modify  the Planning  Commission's  action.

ENVIRONMENT  AL  ANALYSIS:
An environmental  (air quality,  noise,  and traffic  impact)  analysis  (Attachment  C) was conducted  for the
proposed  development,  and based on the studies,  it has been determined  the proposed  project  would  qualify
for  a Categorical  Exemption  under  CEQA  Guidelines  Section  15332  (Class  32 -  Infill  Development
Projects)  and would  not have a significant  environmental  impact.

COMMENTS  FROM  OTHER  DEP ARTMENTS:
Staff routed  the project  for comments  to several  City Departments,  including  the Public  Works  Department.
If the project  is approved,  the comments  received  from the Public  Works  Department  would  be incorporated
as conditions  of approval.

RECOMMENDATION:
Based  on the evidence  presented,  Staff  recommends  that the Planning  Commission  find that the project  is
Categorically  Exempt  from  the CEQA  under  Section  15332,  (Class  32) "Infill  Development  Projects",
make  the required  findings  and requirements  set forth  in the South  Gate Municipal  Code,  and adopt  a
Resolution  to apprOVe  Vesting  Tentative  Tract  Map  No.  84531  associated  with  the 54-unit  townhome
development  at 10130  Adella  Avenue,  subject  to the recommended  conditions  of approval  stipulated  in the
proposed  Resolution  and/or  other conditions  that the Planning  Commission  may wish to impose.

  illumination  for Legacy  Lane and Adella  Avenue.  If deemed  insufficient,  developer  shall design  and
  construct  the necessary  lighting  improvements.  Provide  a photometric  analysis  for Legacy  Lane  and
  Adella  Avenue.  Install  new streetlights  if lighting  distribution  is inadequate.

35. Paint  propeity  address  on the  curb,  in front  of the  proposed  development,  to the  City  and  Fire
  Departments  satisfaction.

36. Close existing  driveway(s)  on Adella  Avenue  and Legacy  Lane, which  will  no longer  be in use as part
  of the new development  and replace  with new curb and gutter and full-width  sidewalk  to match  existing.

  Right-Of-Way  Easements  and Tract  map

37. Developer  shall  prepare  and process  documents  for a Tract  Map.  The Tract  Map  shall  be effective
  when the certificate  of compliance  and deed(s)  has/have  been recorded.  No peri'nit  will  be issued prior
  to recordation.

38. Additional  dedication  may  be required  at the proposed  driveways  to meet  and comply  with  ADA
  requirements.  Proposed  driveways  should  provide  pedestrian  access  across  it with  cross  slope  not
  exceeding  2% and maintain  minimum  width  of 4-foot.

39. Developer  shall submit  the required  document  for the roadway  dedication  or any proposed  easements.
  Comply  with  all requirements  of the Subdivision  Map Act, the City of South Gate Municipal  Code and
  all the applicable  state and local  laws.

  Grading  and Drainage

40. Comply  with  all Federal,  State, and local agency requirements  pertaining  to the Clean Water  Act, which
  establishes  regulations,  set forth  in the Countywide  National  Pollutant  Discharge  Elimination  System
  (NPDES)  Permit.

41. Comply  witli  the City's  Storm  Water  Management  Ordinance.  Implement  all NPDES  requirements
  and Best Management  Practices  during  and after construction.  Provide  and obtain  approval  of a site-
  specific  Erosion  Control  Plan.

42. Submit  a Grading  and Drainage  plans prepared  by a Registered  Civil  Engineer  to the satisfaction  of the
  Public  Works  Department  and Building  Division.  Show  all existing  and proposed  driveways,  curb &
  gutter,  sidewalks,  curb  ramps,  street  trees,  tree  wells,  street  lights,  street  signs,  power  poles,  fire
  hydrants,  utility  boxes,  meters,  curb  drains,  etc. on the plans.  Provide  LID  Plan and calculations
  required  to  address  storm  water  discharge  and  NPDES  requirements  by  City's  Environmental
  Consultant,  John Hunter  and Associates  (See attached  requirements).

45. Provide  a final  detailed  drainage  study (prepared  by a registered/licensed  civil  engineer)  for review  and

48. Iust  control  operations  shall  be perfoimed  by the developer  at the time,  location  and in the amount

  Sewer

49. The developer  shall prepare  a comprehensive  Sewer Capacity  Study signed and stamped  by a registered
  Civil  Engineer  addressing  the sewer needs of the new proposed  site and pay all required  review  fees.
  Initial  deposit  of $761 is required  to initiate  the plan check.  Actual  costs of the review  will  be billed  to
  the developer  as the plan check  progresses.  Based  on the Sewer  Capacity  Study,  the developer  might
  be required  to pay  for  any necessary  sewer  upgrades.  The  limits  of the upgrades  shall  be to the
  downstream  point  of connection  to where  sufficient  capacity  exists.  If in case the sewer connection  is
  made to Los Angeles  County  sewer  system,  the developer  may need to coordinate  and get approval
  from  Los Angeles  County  Sanitation  District  and pay any associated  County  fees.

50. Install  adequate  sewer  lateral(s)  to serve the proposed  development,  and abandon  any existing  sewer
  laterals  at the main line and sewer cleanouts  that will  not be used, to the satisfaction  of the Public  Works
  and Building  & Safety  Departments.  Sewer  laterals  will  be abandoned  in place  with  either  cement
  slurry  backfill  or concrete  bulkhead  plug per City  Standard  Plans.

51. The developer  shall consult  the City Engineer  to detemiine  the sewer location  and design requirements.
  Relocation  of any public  sewer  lines  shall  be subject  to approval  by the City  Engineer.  Pavement
  moratorium  applies.

RE: Request  for Removal  or Modification  of Condition  of Approval  #60 - Case Nos.: APR No.
PL24-0070  & TTM No. PL24-0068-10130  Adella  Avenue  (APN: 6221-026-020)

Dear Gabriel,

This letter  is submitted  as a follow-up  to the April  24, 2025  correspondence  from  Cox, Castle  &
Nicholson  LLP with the subject  Line "Letter  to City re Appear  and Condition  No. 60." As noted  in that
letter,  we respectfully  request  the removal  or modification  of Condition  of Approval  No. 60, which
mandates  the replacement  of the existing  k-rail at the intersection  of AdeLLa Avenue  and Legacy  Lane
with an automated  gate arm or similar  device.

We nOW Write tO supplement  our prior request  With the findings  from the TraffiC and Circulation  Stuoy
completed  by TJW Engineering,  dated  May 16, 2025 (the "TJW Traffic  Study"),  which  confirms  that
the existing  k-rail does not pose a safety  concern  and that the project  does not require  modification
of existing  emergency  access  infrastructure.

  1.  The TJW Traffic  Study  Confirms  Project  Does  Not Create  Unsafe  Conditions

  The TJW TraffiC Stud'y analVzed four intersections and One roadwaV segment, including  all
  driveways  and adjacent  access  points.  It concludes  that  all intersections  will  operate  at

  Level of Service (LOS)A,indicatingfree-flowtraffic  with no congestion. The project 8enerates
  only 364 daily trips,  including  22 AM and 28 PM peak-hour  trips,  which  do not rise to any
  threshold  of significance  under  local  policy  or well-accepted  standard  for potential  impacts
  to intersection  operation.

  Further,  the analysis  confirmed  ttiat the existing  stopping  Sight distance  (SSD) along  Legacy
  Lane  meets  Caltrans  safety  requirements,  and that  pedestrian  and  cyclist  visibility  and
  access  are preserved.  The report  explicitly  states:

  "The proposed  project  is not anticipated  to affect  pedestrian  or bicycie  safety  atong
  Legacy Lane or the project  frontage...  Low-speed  conditions,  existing  sidewalks,  and
  driveway  sightlines  support  a safe environment  for al/ users.

  3121  Michelson  Drive,  Suite  150,  Irvine,  CA 92612

  2-RS314
   The report  also  accounted  for a permanent  barrier  in place  between  Adella  Avenue  and
  ALdrich  Road,  such  as the  existing  K-Rail,  and concluded  that  even with  the  road  being
  closed,  there  was no safety  concern  for emergency  vehicles  needing  an additional  point  of
  access.

  2.  DenserProjectWasPreviouslyApprovedwithPermanentBollards
  The previously  approved  Legacy Apartments  project,  consisting  of 78 units,  was not required
  to remove  the k-rail  and install  an automated  gate.  Instead,  it was conditioned  to install
  permanent  bolLards,  maintaining  restricted  access  at AdelLa Avenue.  The City concluded
  that  the  denser,  more  impactful  project  posed  no  emergency  access  issues  with  a
  permanent  barrierin  place.

  3.  LACFD  Review  Confirms  Emergency  Access  is Sufficient
  As confirmed  in the City's  deemed  complete  letter,  the Los Angeles  County  Fire Department
  (LACFD) was responsible  for reviewing  emergency  access  and circulation.  LACFD's  April 7,
  2025 letter  and site plan stamp  identify  only one public  safety  requirement:  the installation
  of a fire  hydrant  on Legacy  Lane.  No modifications  to the  k-rail  were  requested.  LACFD
  cleared  the  project  for  public  hearing,  confirming  compliance  with  emergency  access
  standards.'

  4.  No Nexus  or Rough  Proportionality  for K-Rail  Removal
  Because  there  is no reasonable  relationship  between  the replacement  of the k-rail  and the
  prOjeCt,  requiring  the appliCant  tO remOVe Or replaCe  the  k-rail  iS  net legally  supportable
  under the No(ran/Dolan  or Koontz  standards.  There is no nexus between  the project's  actuaL
  impacts  and the requested  infrastructure  change,  nor is the requirement  proportional  to the
  project's  traffic  or  circulation  footprint.  As  such,  the  condition  would  constitute  an
  unconstitutional  exaction.

Dear  Mr.  Patterson,

TJW Engineering,  Inc. (TJW) is pleased to submit this Traffic and Circulation  Study for the proposed  project
located at the southeast corner of Legacy Lane and Adella Lane in the City of South Gate, California. The proposed
project is for the construction  of 54 residential  townhomes.  The purpose of this Traffic and Circulation  Study is
to provide a summary review of the potential  traffic impacts of the proposed project.

PROPOSED PROJECT

The site for the proposed project is located at the southeast corner of Legacy Lane and Adella Lane in the City of
South Gate, California. The proposed  project is for the construction  of 54 residential  townhomes.  The site will
be accessible via three proposed full-access driveways along Legacy Lane. Existing street parking on Legacy Lane
will remain available. See Appendix A for a copy of the project site plan.

STUDY  AREA  AND  PARAMETERS

This study reviews four (4) study intersections  and one (1) roadway  segment.

Driveway  Intersections:

  Project Driveway #1 / Legacy Lane
  Legacy High School Softball  Field Driveway #1 / Legacy Lane
  Proposed Driveway #2 / Legacy Lane.

Roadway Segment:

EXISTING  CONDITIONS

The two (2) Existing studyintersections  include two (2) gated driveways  for the parking lot of the Legacy  High
School Softball  Field, opposite  the proposed  project.  Street-parking  and sidewalks  exist along both sides of
Legacy Lane. A bike path exists along the Los Angeles River which lies approximately  500 feet to the east of
the project site.

Traffic volumes at the Existing study intersections  and roadway segment were collected  on Wednesday,  April
30, 2025 over a 12-hour  period  between  7:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Pedestrian  and cyclist volumes  were also
collected  along the roadway segment.  The data collected  is provided  in Appendix  B.

Existing Traffic Volumes

At Intersection  2, the gate for the westerly  Softball  Field Driveway  #1 was observed  to be closed until
approximately  3:00 PM. Therefore,  any vehicles  counted  at Intersection  2 before  3:00 PM were vehicles
traveling  through  on Legacy Lane. During  the 12-hour  observation  period,  a total  of 277 vehicles  were

counted  at Intersection  2 including  29 during the AM peak hour and 69 during the PM peak hour. Between
3:00 PM - 7:00 PM when the gate was opened,  a total of 52 vehicles were observed  entering  the parking lot
and 56 exiting.  The gate for the easterly  Driveway  #2 was observed  to be closed for the entire 12-hour
observation period. A total of 184 vehicles were counted  traveling  on Legacy Lane between  the 90-degree
curve and Burtis Street.

Existing Pedestrian and Cydist Volumes

Over the 12-hour  observation  period, a total of 62 pedestrians  and 49 cyclists mere counted  on Legacy Lane
between  the two Legacy High School Softball  Field driveways.  Of the pedestrians,  21 were observed walking
along the parking  lot frontage,  27 along the proposed  project  frontage,  and 14 along both sides of the
roadway  due to crossing mid-block.  The largest number  of pedestrians,  23 total,  observed  during a 1-hour
period  occurred  between  8:15 AM - 9:15 AM. The cyclists  were  evenly  distributed  with  24 traveling
eastbound and 25 westbound. The largest number  of cyclists, 10, observed  in either direction  during a 1-hour
period occurred between 4:30 PM - 5:30 PM.

Analysis Methodology

Operations  for  unsignalized  intersections  are evaluated  using the  methodology  of the  Highway  Capacity
Manual,  7'h Edition  (HCM)  (Transportation  Research  Board,  2022).  The HCM methodology  uses Level of
Service (LOS) to express the delay time forintersection  approaches  and to describe  the corresponding  quality
of flow  on roadways  and intersections.  LOS is commonly  used to describe  the quality  of flow  on roadways
and at intersections  using a range  of LOS from  LOS A, free  flow  with  little  congestion,  to LOS F, severely
congested  conditions.

daily  and AM  and  PM peak  hour  trip  generation  of the  proposed  project.  The  project  is anticipated  to

at a cul-de-sac.  It is presumed  that vehicles  observed  traveling  east on Legacy Lane past Intersection  2 during
the 12-hour  observation  period  were traveling  to and from  the business  to the immediate  east of the project
site.

STOPPING SIGHT DISTANCE ANALYSIS

Stopping  sight  distance  (SSD) was evaluated  for the  proposed  residential  driveways  along  Legacy Lane in
accordance  with  the Caltrans  Highway  Design Manual  (HDM).  Per HDM Table 201.1, the required  SSD for a
design speed of 25 miles per hour is 150 feet. This distance  represents  the minimum  length  of roadway  that
must be visible  to a driver  to allow  for safe and complete  stopping  in response  to an object  in the roadway.
The design of Legacy Lane ensures  that the minimum  SSD is maintained  in both directions  of travel  from  each
driveway  location.  The attached  sight distance  exhibit  illustrates  the available  SSD along the roadway.  Exhibit

within  the designated  Area and then annually  remitting  those funds back to the BusinesS Improvement
District  ("BID").  Section  2.64.040  (Uses and Purpose),  of Title  2 (Licenses-Business  Regulations)  of
the South Gate Municipal  Code states that the funds collected  by the City and remitted  to the BID  can
only be used for the following  purposes:

  Decoration  of any public  place in the area;
  Promotion  of public  events which  are to take place on or in public  places in the area;
  and
  C.  The general promotion  of retail trade activities  in the area.

The  City's  Municipal  Code  also  requires  that  the  Tweedy  Mile  Advisory  Board  ("Board")
submit  an Annual  Report  to the City  Council  no later  than  June  Ist of each year. The Annual
Report  shall  specify  the  expenses,  services,  activities,  and  programs  to  be  funded  by  the
assessment  for  the upcoming  fiscal  year(s),  in accordance  with  the requirements  of  Sections
36530  and 36533  of the California  Streets  and Highways  Code.  Said Code also requires  the City
Council  to approve  the Aru'iual  Report,  and, after,  shall  adopt  a Resolution  declaring  the City's
intention  to levy  an annual  assessment  for the fiscal  year and schedule  a Public  Hearing  to allow
public  testimony  regarding  the proposed  assessment.

The Board  approved  the attached  Tweedy  Mile  Advisory  Board  Aru'iual  Report  (Attachment  A).
Staff  recommend  that the City  Council  approve  the Annual  Report  which  includes  a program
budget  for Fiscal  Year  2025/26.  In addition  to the Annual  Report,  staff also recommend  that the
City  Council  adopt  the proposed  Resolution  declaring  the City's  intention  to levy  and collect
assessments  for  Fiscal  Year  2025/26  (Attachment  B)  and approve  the scheduling  of a Public
Hearing  for June 24, 2025.  Together,  the Resolution  and Annual  Report  are the initial  steps to
levy the proposed  assessments  and approve  the program  budget  for Fiscal  Year 2025/26.

  *  HdL (Consultant) will establish a web portal for businesses to submit a new application,  renewal, or pay a balance
  due  for a business license permit.

 ANALYSIS:  The  proposed  Agreement  was  procured  through  a formal,  publicly  advertised
competitive  bid process  in accordance  with  the City's  purchasing  policies  and applicable  public
contracting  regulations.  All  bidders  were  evaluated  for responsiveness-completeness  of their
submissions,  adherence  to  the  bid  specifications,  and  compliance  with  all  mandatory
requirements-and  for responsibility,  including  demonstrated  experience,  financial  stability,  and
safety  record.  The award  criterion  focused  solely  on the lowest  Base Bid  ai'nount  submitted  by a
responsible  and responsive  firm.

Following  bid opening  and evaluation,  Superior  Pavement  Markings,  Inc. emerged  as the lowest
responsible  and responsive  bidder,  offering  the most  cost-effective  solution  at a Base  Bid  of
$94,511.  Their  proposal  met all technical  specifications  for materials,  application  methods,  and
project  timeline,  and their  past  performance  on  comparable  thermoplastic  striping  contracts
underscores  their  capacity  to deliver  high-quality  results.  Consequently,  staff  recommends  that
the Agreement  be awarded  to Superior  Pavement  Markings,  Inc. in the amount  of $94,511  for the
timely  and cost-efficient  completion  of the Citywide  striping  project.

BACKGROUND:  The  City's  roadway  network  has  over  125  miles  of  streets.  The  street
pavements  are marked  with  striping  road  lanes,  pavement  legends  and crosswalks  that require
thermoplastic  material.  A comprehensive  field  survey  of major  streets  citywide  identified  faded
and deteriorated  condition  of striping  and pavement  markings  on the streets  selected  for  this
project.  Attachment  C shows  the locations  where  work  will  be perfornned,  noting  a noteworthy
amount  of work  will  be performed  on Southern  Ave  and State Street.

The proposed  project  will  reapply  durable  thermoplastic  striping  citywide-refreshing  lane lines,
legends,  and crosswalks-to  restore  high-visibility  pavement  graphics  and significantly  enhance
both  driver  awareness  and  pedestrian  safety.  In  addition,  the  long-lasting  properties  of
thernnoplastic  materials  will  reduce  maintenance  frequency  and lower  lifecycle  costs  over  the
next seven to ten years.

An  Agreement  is necessary  to start  construction.  On February  20, 2025,  staff  advertised  the
Notice  Inviting  Bids  for  construction  on Planet  Bids.  The  Project  was also advertised  on the
City's  website.  On March  13, 2025,  the City  held  a bid opening  at the City  Clerk's  Office.  Five
bids were received  and Superior  Pavement  Markings,  Inc. provided  the lowest  bid in the amount
of $94,511.  The engineer's  estimate  is $157,700. After  completion  of the bid analysis,  Superior
Pavement  Markings,  Inc.,  was confirn'ied  to be the lowest  responsible  bidder,  and their  bid was
confirmed  to be responsive.

Staff  checked  the contractor's  references.  Having  been in existence  as a general  contractor  for 25
years,  Superior  Pavement  Markings,  Inc.,  has the necessary  experience  to perform  the work
required  for the Project.  Superior  Pavement  Markings,  Inc.  has successfully  completed  similar
projects  for the Cities  of San Dimas,  Arcadia  and Irvine.

Pursuant  to the guidelines  of the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  ("CEQA"),  the Project
was  categorically  exempt  under  Title  14  of  the  California  Code  of  Regulations,  Existing
Facilities  Section  15301  Class (c): Existing  highways  and streets,  sidewalks,  gutters,  bicycle  and
pedestrian  trails,  and similar  facilities.

  PURPOSE:  To receive  approval  for a Lease Agreement  with  Lease  Servicing  Center,  Inc.,  dba
  NCL  Governrnent  Capital  to  replace  aging  Parking  Enforcement  vehicles  for  the  Police
  Department  and lease one 2025 Ford Maverick  vehicle.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a 5-year  Lease  Agreement  with  Lease  Servicing  Center,  Inc.  dba  NCL
  Government  Capital  ("NCL")  for the lease of one 2025 Ford Maverick  vehicle  to be used
  as a Parking Enforcement vehicle for the Police  Department  in the amount  of $7,785  per
  year for a total amount  of $39,425, including  a $500 closing  fee;
  b. Approving  lease payments  in the amount  of $7,785  to be budgeted  annually  for five (5)
  years in the General Fund starting  in Fiscal  Year 2024/2025  and a $500 closing  fee in
  Fiscal Year 2024/2025;
  c.  Approving  a Purchase  Order Agreement  with  Cornrnline  Inc., for the purchase  and
  installation  of necessary  emergency  equipment  and MDC  to outfit  the Parking
  Enforcement  vehicle  in the amount  of $14,035;  and
  d. Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the lease Agreement  and any other documents  that  may

  be necessary  to acquire  the vehicles  in a form  acceptable  to the City Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Funds  for this purchase  were included  in the Fiscal  Year  ("FY")  2024/25
  General  Fund Budget  (Account  #100-505-21-6310)  for the first  aru'iual lease payment  of $8,285,
  inclusive  of the $500 closing  fee. Funds  for the cost of purchasing  and installing  all the necessary
  equipment  were included  in the 2024/25  Capital  Asset & Equipment  Replacement  Fund (Account
  #523-505-21-9003).  The remaining  four  annual  lease payments  will  be in the amount  of $7,785
  and will  be funded  through  the General  Fund  (Account  #100-505-21-6310)  for  a 5-year  total
  amount  of $39,425.

  ANALYSIS:  This  lease  agreement  was  explored  to allow  the Police  Department  to procure
  vehicles  for  use by Parking  Enforcement  personnel.  A 2007  Ford  Escape  (Unit  126)  will  be
  replaced  if the lease agreement  is approved.  Unit  126 had to be removed  from  service  in 2024 due
  to significant  mechanical  issues that could  not be repaired  due to discontinued  replacement  parts.

 BACKGROUND:  The City  of South Gate ("City")  researched  procurement  options  for fleet
vehicles  and discovered  that other agencies  had completed  open, fair, transparent,  and
competitive  procurement  processes,  complying  with  bid requirements  set forth by our Municipal
Code. The City  reviewed  the contract  options  and determined  that the Sourcewell  Master  Vehicle
contract  #01 1620-NCL  with  Lease Servicing  Center,  Inc., dba NCL  Government  Capital,
provided  the best value to the City.  South  Gate Municipal  Code Section  1.54.510(D)  provides  an
alternative  procurement  method  by permitting  the City  to purchase  or otherwise  obtain  services,
supplies,  materials,  equipment,  and labor with  other agencies  through  cooperative  contracts
(piggybacking).  This  alternative  procurement  method  can save time  and reduce  costs through
economies  of scale by purchasing  under  existing  contracts  from  different  agencies  on a voluntary
and selective  basis.

  appropriating  $40,000  to Account  Number  232-541-21-6204  (Law  Enforcement  Grants-
  Homeland  Security  Grant  - Small  Tools  and Equipment);  and
  d.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to execute  the State Homeland  Security  Grant  Program
  Subrecipient  Agreement  for Grant  Year 2023.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  on the General  Fund  and no requirement  for the
  City  to match  these grant funds.  The total  amount  of funding  allocated  to the City  for Fiscal  Year
  2025/26  is $40,000.  The grant  will  cover  the one-time  costs associated  with  the purchase  and
  installation  of the Automated  License  Plate Reader  ("ALPR")  cameras.  Ongoing  costs related  to
  the operation  of the cameras  will  be funded  from  Asset Forfeiture  funds.

  fixed  points  throughout  the city,  as well  as mounting  them  on police  department  vehicles.  This
  technology  will  allow  police  department  personnel  to coordinate  public  safety  responses  when

alcohol abuse in the workplace. These dangers include death and injury to the employee, co-workers, or the
public resulting from accidents, dereliction of duty, poor judgment and carelessness.  Substance abuse also
results in lost productivity, reduced efficiency, and increased absenteeism  by the substance abuser and
inteferes with the job performance of employees who do not use illegal or unauthorized substances. [Section
8355(b) (1)]

California law prohibits the unlawful manufacture,  dispensation, possession,  or illegal use of a controlled
substance. That prohibition extends to all places  and includes the worksite  of California state employees.

satisfactory completion of a drug abuse assistance or rehabilitation program. [Section 8355(b)(4)]

counseling and rehabilitation  services. The EAP is available to all agency employees. Procedures exist to

  SHSP  and  UASI  Funding  Priorities
  Given  the evolving  national  security  threat  landscape,  DHS/FEMA  has evaluated  the national
  risk profile  and set priorities  that help inform  appropriate  allocation  of scarce security  dollars.
  In assessing  the national  risk profile  for FY 2023,  six National  Priority  Areas  pose the most
  concern.  Iue  to the riniqrie  threats  that the nation  faces in 2023,  DHS/FEMA  has determined
  that recipients  should  allocate  a total  of 30% of their  SHSP  and UASI  award  funds  across
  these six priority  areas. As indicated  below,  five  of the priorities  have minimum  spend
  reqriirements  totaling  15% of SHSP  and UASI  awards.  Recipients  will  have the flexibility  to
  allocate  the remaining  15% across the priorities.  The following  are the six priority  areas for
  FY 2023,  along  with  the minimum  corresponding  percentage  of SHSP  and UASI  funds  that
  each recipient  will  be required  to allocate:

  1)  Enhancing  the protection  of soft targets/crowded  places  - 3%
  2)  Enhancing  information  and intelligence  sharing  and analysis  - 3%
  3)  Combating  domestic  violent  extremism  - 3%
  4)  Enhancing  cybersecurity  - no minimum  percent
  5)  Enhancing  community  preparedness  and resilience  - 3%
  6)  Enhancing  election  security  - 3%

  OPSG  Allocations
  For FY 2023,  DHS/FEMA  will  award  OPSG  funds  based on risk  and the aiiticipated
  effectiveness  of the proposed  use of grant  funds  upon  completion  of the application  review

  process.  The FY 2023  0PSG  risk assessment  is designed  to identify  the risk to border

  security  and to assist with  the distribution  of funds  for the grant program.  Funding  under

  OPSG  is distributed  based on the risk to the security  of the border  and the effectiveness  of

  the proposed  projects.  Entities  eligible  for funding  are the state, local,  and tribal  law

  enforcement  agencies  that are located  along  the border  of the United  States.  DHS/FEMA  will

  make final  award  determinations  based upon a review  of the anticipated  effectiveness  of the

  state's  application  as described  in Section  D, below.  The  THIRA/SPR  process  is not

  required  for  OPSG.

  For the purposes  of OPSG,  the risk is defined  as the potential  for an adverse  outcome

  assessed as a function  of threats,  vulnerabilities,  and consequences  associated  with  an

  incident,  event,  or occurrence.

  Based  upon  ongoing  intelligence  analysis  and extensive  security  reviews,  DHS/CBP

  continues  to focus  the bulk  of OPSG  funds  based upon risk analyses.  The risk model  used to

  allocate  OPSG  funds  considers  the potential  risk that certain  threats  pose to border  security

  and estimates  the relative  risk faced  by a given  area. In evaluating  risk,  DHS/CBP  considers

  intelligence,  situational  awareness,  criminal  trends,  and statistical  data specific  to each of the

  border  sectors,  and the potential  impacts  that these threats  pose to the security  of the border

  area. For vulnerability  and consequence,  DHS/CBP  considers  the expected  impact  and

  consequences  of successful  border  events  occurring  in specific  areas.

  Threat  and vulnerability  are evaluated  based on specific  operational  data from  DHS/CBP.

  Threat  components  present  in each of the sectors  are cised to determine  the overall  threat

  score. These  components  are terrorism,  criminal  aliens,  drug trafficking  organizations,  and

  alien  smuggling  organizations.

  Per section 2006 of the Homeland  Security  Act of 2002, as amended  (6 U.S.C.  § 607),

  is requiring  that  at least 35%  of grant  funding  appropriated  under  HSGP  is  used for
  LETPA.  DHS/FEMA  meets this requirement,  in part, by requiring  all recipients  allocate  at
  least 35% of the combined  HSGP funds allocated  under SHSP and UASI  towards  LETPAs,
  as defined  in 6 U.S.C.  § 607. The LETPA  allocation  can be from SHSP, UASI,  or  both. The
  35% LETPA  allocation  may be met by fimding  projects  in any combination  of the six
  National  Priority  Areas identified  above and any other investments.  The 35% LETPA
  allocation  requirement  is in addition  to the 80% pass-through  reqriirement  to local units of
  government  and tribes, referenced  below.  The Preparedness  Grants Manual  and Information
  Bulletin  (IB) 473 include  additional  information  on project  selection  considerations  and
  allowable  activities  for LETPA  investments.  Also see Section D.l4.f  "Allowable  Costs
  Matrix."

  The National  Prevention  Framework  describes  those activities  that sliould  be executed  ripon
  tlie discovery  of intelligence  or information  regarding  an imminent  threat to the homeland,  to
  thwart  an initial  or follow-on  teirorist  attack and provides  guidance  to ensure the Nation  is
  prepared  to identify,  prevent,  avoid, or stop a threatened  or actual act of terrorism.  Activities
  oritlined  in the National  Prevention  Framework  are eligible  for use as LETPA-focused  funds.

  Framework  activities  are also eligible.  All other terrorism  prevention  activities  proposed  for

  E.  Application  Review  Information
  1.  Application  Evaluation  Criteria
  a.  Programmatic  Criteria
  s.  RISK METHODOLOGY
  The risk methodology  determines  the relative  risk of tertaorism  faced  by a given  area
  considering  the potential  risk of terrorism  to people,  critical  infrastructure,  and economic
  security.  The analysis  includes,  but is not limited  to, threats  from  violent  domestic
  extremists,  international  terrorist  groups,  and individuals  inspired  by terrorists  abroad.  See
  the Preparedness  Grants  Manual  for additional  information  on the risk methodology.

  NOTE:  The THIRA/SPR  process  is separate  from  the risk methodology  and its results  do
  not affect  grant  allocations.

  The Risk  Methodology  is used to inform  allocations  under  HSGP.  For more  information  on
  the SHSP,  UASI,  and OPSG  allocation  processes,  please  see Section  B. l of this NOFO,
  "Available  Funding  for the NOFO."

  n.  APPLICATION  EVALUATION  CRITERIA
  FEMA  will  evaluate  the FY 2023  HSGP  applications  for completeness,  adherence  to
  programmatic  guidelines,  and anticipated  effectiveness  of the proposed  investments.
  FEMA's  review  will  include  verification  that each U and project:

  *  Aligns  with  at least one core capability  identified  in the Goal;
  *  Demonstrates  how  investments  support  building  capability  and/or  closing  capability
  gaps or sustaining  capabilities  identified  in the THIRA/SPR  process;  and
  *  Supports  a NIMS-typed  resource  and whether  those assets are deployable/shareable  to
  support  emergency  or disaster  operations  per existing  EMAC  agreements.

2.  Review  and Selection  Process
 a.  SHSP  and UASI
  All proposed  investments  will  undergo  a federal review  by DHS/FEMA  to verify
  compliance  with all administrative  and eligibility  criteria  identified  in the NOFO.  The
  federal  review  will  be conducted  by FEMA  HQ Preparedness  Officers.  FEMA  HQ
  Preparedness  Officers  will  use a checklist  to verify  compliance  with  all administrative  and
  eligibility  criteria  identified  in the NOFO.  Recipients  must be able to demonstrate  how
  investments  suppoit  building  capability  and/or closing  capability  gaps  or  sustaining
  capabilities  identified in the THIRA/SPR  process. Us will  be reviewed  at both the
  investment  and project level.

  Emergency  commrinications  investments  will  be jointly  reviewed  by FEMA  and CISA's
  Emergency  Communications  Division  (ECD)  to verify  compliance  with  SAFECOM
  Guidance  on Emergency  Communications  Grants (SAFECOM  Guidance).  FEMA  and ECD
  will  coordiiiate  directly  with the recipient  on any compliance  concerns  and will  provide
  technical  assistance  as necessary to help ensure  full compliance.

  percentages

2.  Pass-Through  Requirements
  Awards  made  to the SAA  for HSGP  catry  additional  statutorily  mandated  pass-through

  requirements.  Pass-through  is defined  as an obligation  on the part  of the  SAA  to make  funds

  available  to local  units  of government,  combinations  of local  units,  tribal  governments,  or

  other  specific  groups  or organizations.  These  entities  are defined  at 6 U.S.C.  § 101(13)  as:

  *  A corinty,  municipality,  city,  town,  township,  local  public  authority,  school  district,

  special  district,  intrastate  district,  council  of governments  (regardless  of whether  the

  council  of goveriiments  is incorporated  as a nonprofit  corporation  rinder  State  law),

  regional  or interstate  government  entity,  or agency  or instrumentality  of a local

  government.
  *  An  Indian  tribe  or authorized  tribal  organization,  or in Alaska  a Native  village  or

  Alaska  Regional  Native  Corporation.

  *  A rural  community,  rmincorporated  town  or village,  or other  public  entity.

8. Notes  on  Personnel  Cost:

In qeneral,  costs  associated  with:

€ Work performed  under contract  for a specific  deliverable  DOES  NOT count against  the
  personnel  cap, however,
€ Work  performed  under  contract  for an undefined  period,  such as for personnel  costs
  supporting  operational  activities,  including  general  planning,  training  or exercise
  activities  DO count  against  the personnel  cap  and
€ Work  performed  by all non-contractor  personnel,  including  for full- or part-time  staff and
  operational  overtime  DO count  against  the personnel  cap.

The followinq  examples  would  not count  towards  the personnel  cap:

€ Vendor  installation  of a radio tower;
€ Vendor  training  on new equipment  purchased;
€ Contractor  hired to create  an Emergency  Operations  Plan;
€ Contractor  hired to provide  deliveries  of ICS 400; and
€ Contractor  hired to assist with planning,  training,  evaluating,  and reporting  the
  effectiveness  of a specific  exercise.

The followinq  examples  would  count  towards  the personnel  cap:
€ Contractor  hired to be the State's  WMD  training  instructor  with no specific  deliverables
  under contract:
€ Contractor  hired to facilitate  unidentified  number  of exercises  throughout  the
  performance  period
€ Contractor  hired to be the part-time auditor of Homeland  Security  Grants  throughout  the year; and
€ Contractor  hired to be an intelligence analyst.

 ANALYSIS:  The proposed  CCO No. 2, in the amount  of $56,600,  will  authorize  the re-striping
of intersections  along Tweedy  Boulevard,  California  Avenue  and Southern  Avenue,  with  durable
thernnoplastic  material.  The  proposed  work  includes  re-striping  crosswalks,  and  pavement
markings.

CCO No. 2 is priced  consistent  with  the bid pricing.  By leveraging  the unit bid costs, this change
order  delivers  cost-effective,  long-lasting  pavement  graphics  extending  marking  life  to seven
years  or more  and  reducing  aru'iual  maintenance  needs  while  significantly  improving  both
daytime  and nighttime  visibility  for motorists  and pedestrians

BACKGROUND:  The  City's  roadway  network  spans more  than  125 miles  of streets,  all of
which  depend  on high-visibility  pavement  legends,  crosswalks,  and lane delineations  to promote
safe and efficient  traffic  flow.  These  essential  markings  utilize  durable  thermoplastic  materials,
offering  superior  reflectivity  and extended  service  life  compared  to conventional  paint.  This
project  will  fully  refurbish  existing  crosswalks  and pavement  legends  with  new  thermoplastic
applications  and  will  refresh  all  lane  lines  and  centerlines  to  uphold  consistent  visibility
standards  and full  compliance  with  MUTCD  guidelines.

On May  23, 2023,  the City  Council  awarded  the Thermoplastic  Striping  of Streets  Citywide
contract  to WGJ  in the amount  of $100,860.  Work  commenced  on June 22, 2023,  and concluded
on August  18,  2023.  During  this  initial  phase,  it was  necessary  to administratively  approve

Change  Order  No.  1, totaling  $31,732  to cover  the  actual  quantities  of thermoplastic  work
performed  that  exceeded  the  original  bid  estimates.  This  supplemental  authorization  ensured
uninternipted  progress  and delivered  immediate  safety  enhancements  without  delay.

Construction  of the project  was completed  under  budget,  allowing  additional  funding  to be used
for restriping  crosswalks  and pavement  markings  on other  City  streets.  Staff  conducted  a field
survey  to identify  additional  locations  where  the pavement  was in good  condition  and suitable
for restriping.  This  survey  took  time  to complete.  Once potential  locations  were identified,  staff
re-initiated  the construction  scheduling  process  with  the contractor.  However,  WGJ  had a full
schedule  due to commitments  in other jurisdictions,  and also faced a shortage  of materials,  which
further  delayed  efforts  to reschedule  the work.  As a result,  the construction  contract  was put on
hold  and the start date was postponed.

Construction  is planned  to start on May  26, 2025,  and be completed  within  ten (10)  working
days.

SUBJECT:  PURCHASE  ORDER  TO  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY  DEPARTMENT  OF
PUBLIC  WORKS,  SERVICE  REQUEST  N0.  272919  FOR  EMERGENCY  CALL  OUT  AT
THE  INTERSECTION  OF SANTA  ANA  STREET  AND  PALM/SEVILLE

PURPOSE:  Approve  a purchase  order to fund  Service  Request  No. 272919  with  the Los Angeles
County  Department  of Public  Works  ("LACDPW")  for emergency  traffic  signal repairs  performed
at the intersection  of Santa Ana  Street  and Palm/Seville.  LACDPW  responded  to an emergency
call-out  and has completed  the necessary  work  to restore  the traffic  signal  to full  operation.  The
repairs  were considered  time-sensitive  and essential  for public  safety.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Purchase  Order  for the Los  Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Works
  ("County"),  Service  Request  No. 272919  to fund emergency  call-out  traffic  signal  repairs
  at the intersection  of Santa  Ana  Street  and Palm/Seville,  for  an amount  not to exceed
  $60,500;  and
  b. Authorizing  the City  Manager  to execute  the Purchase  Order,  in a form  approved  by the
  City Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There is no impact  on the General  Fund.  The proposed  Purchase  Order  is in
the amount of $60,500. It will be funded with  $11,500  in Gas Tax  and $49,000  in Measure  R
Funds, budgeted for the Fiscal Year 2024/25.

ANALYSIS:  The traffic  signal  system  at the intersection  of Santa Aria  Street  and Palm/Seville
sustained  damage  due  to vandalism,  resulting  in  compromised  wiring  at multiple  pull  box
locations.  As  a result,  the intersection  became  inoperative,  creating  a public  safety  hazard.  In
alignment  with  the City  of South  Gate's  ("City")  policy  to prioritize  urgent  infrastructure  repairs
that  impact  public  health  and safety,  the Public  Works  Department  coordinated  an expedited
response  to restore  signal  functionality  in collaborations  with  LACDPW.

Under  the  City's  existing  agreement  with  LACDPW,  the  County  provides  both  routine  and
extraordinary  maintenance  for designated  traffic  signal  intersections  within  South Gate. Given  the
urgency  of the situation  and the County's  established  role  as the City's  contracted  maintenance
provider,  Public  Works  is recommending  that the City  Council  approve  a sole-source  Purchase

  1

  631
 Order  to Los Angeles  County  Public  Works  in an amount  not to exceed  $60,500  for emergency
traffic  signal  repair  work  that  has already  been  completed.  The  work  was  performed  as an
emergency  call-out  to promptly  restore  full  signal  operation  and address  a critical  public  safety
issue. This action  ensures proper  authorization  and funding  for the completed  work  and aligns  with
the City's  commitment  to maintaining  safe and functional  infrastructure  for the benefit  of the
public.

BACKGROUND:  The  City  of  South  Gate  Public  Works  Department  maintains  93 traffic
signalized  intersections  throughout  the City,  which  are equipped  with  safety  lights,  illuminated
street name signs, video  vehicle  detection  systems,  battery  back-up  systems,  and speed awareness
signs. These intersections  are critical  components  ofthe  City's  infrastructure,  contributing  to public
safety  and the smooth  flow  of traffic.

Maintenance,  service,  and repair  of these intersections  are carried  out through  a combination  of
in-house  staff and contract  services.  In collaboration  with  agencies  such as Los Angeles  County
Public  Works,  the City  ensures that its traffic  signal  systems  are functioning  optimally.

Recently,  the electrical  wiring  for the traffic  signal  system  at the intersection  of Santa Aria  Street
and Palm/Seville  was vandalized,  rendering  the signal  inoperative  and the intersection  dark. If not
promptly  addressed,  this  condition  poses  a significant  risk  to public  safety,  may  contribute  to
increased  traffic  congestion,  and raises the potential  for traffic  accidents.  Timely  repairs  are critical
to restoring  safe travel  conditions  and ensuring  the continued  reliability  of the City's  transportation
infrastructure

The fee proposal  submitted  by Los Angeles  County  Public  Works  for the necessary  repairs  was
thoroughly  reviewed  by City  staff.  After  careful  evaluation,  it was determined  that the proposed
costs align  with  industry  standards  for similar  repair  work.  Given  the urgency  of the situation  and
the County's  established  expertise,  the proposal  is considered  reasonable  and appropriate  for the
scope of work  required.  Staff has confirmed  that the costs reflect  fair pricing  for the services  to be
rendered,  ensuring  the City  is receiving  value in line with  prevailing  market  rates.

PURPOSE:  To award  a professional  services  agreement  ("Agreement")  to De Novo  Plaru'iing  Group
("De  Novo")  for  consulting  services  to address  three  important  issues:  (1)  an ordinance  amendment
regarding  land  uses;  (2)  land  use  improvements  surrounding  two  future  transit  centers;  and  (3)
enhancements  to commercial  corridors  to encourage  new  businesses  and development.

An  environmental  review  to analyze  potential  impacts  created  by  an ordinance  or other  actions  is
required  pursuant  to the California  Environmental  Quality  Act  ("CEQA")  Guidelines.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The  City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  an Agreement  with  De Novo  for planning  and environmental  services;  and
  b.  Authorizing  the Mayor  to execute  the Agreement  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  According  to the  consultant's  proposal,  planning  and  environmental  services
would  cost $524,905,  which  would  be paid  from  the General  Fund.

ALIGNMENT  WITH  COUNCIL  GOALS:  The  FY  2024-2025  Annual  Action  Plans  supports  the
City  Council  goals  of creating  and protecting  strong  and  sustainable  neighborhoods  by  supporting
projects  and programs  that benefit  low-and  moderate-income  residents  of South  Gate.

BACKGROUND:  On  April  16,  2024,  the  Planning  Commission  ("Cornrnission")  held  a public
hearing  on a similar  item  to consider  a Zone  Code  Amendment  to modify  Title  11,  Chapter  11.21  of
the South  Gate Municipal  Code  to revise  the City  of South  Gates's  ("City")  Ordinance  pertaining  to
building  areamaximums  forwarehousing  landuse  types.  The Cornrnission  considered  two resolutions:
the first,  Resolution  No. 2024-02A,  recornrnended  to the City  Council  that the City's  Zoning  Code  be
revised  to  eliminate  size  limitations  on  warehouses  in  the  City's  Urban  Mixed-Use  Zones  and
Commercial  Industrial  Zones;  the second,  Resolution  No.  2024-02B,  would  direct  staff  to study  the
matter  further  and return  to the Commission  later  with  recommendations.  The  Cornrnission  voted  to
deny  both  resolutions  by a vote  of 3-2 and 5-0, respectively.

 On May 28, 2024, City  Council  considered  an appeal of the Planning  Comi'nission's  denial  of the Zone
Code  Amendment.  City  Council  received  public  coini'nents  from  members  of the public.  At  the
conclusion  of the hearing,  the City  Council  voted,  3-2, to direct  staff to explore  alternatives  of having
a cap on warehouse  use in the City,  and further  research  the issue on industrial  uses. Subsequently,
staff  engaged  the services  of Kosmont  Companies  ("Kosmont")  to provide  guidance  on what  other
cities  are doing  in regard  to industrial  use policies.

On August  21, 2024,  City  Council  received  apresentation  from the Kosmont  Companies  ("Kosmont")
on  an industrial  land  use study.  The City  retained  Kosmont  to research  various  policies  adopted  by
select cities. While  there are a few cities that prohibit  new warehouses,  most create policies  to generate
substantial  revenue  from  new warehouses  to offset  traffic  and other impacts  and help achieve  a better
balance  between  businesses  and residential  neighborhoods.  The  City's  industrial  land  is in high
demand  because  the City  is in a prime  location  near Port of LA  and Long  Beach.  The growth  of e-
commerce  also lures  businesses  and developers  who  are seeking  opportunities  for new warehouses
and distribution  centers  in the City.  The  City  has a number  of industrially  zoned  parcels  that  are
suitable  for redevelopment,  but  questions  arose  as to what  will  be acceptable  uses in the future.
Currently,  there are industrial  areas in the City  that are blighted  and underutilized  and landowners  and
businesses  are interested  in bringing  industrial  land uses, including  warehousing,  to revitalize  these
areas.  Industrial  development  with  warehousing  can create  opportunities  for landowners  and create
jobs,  but they can also create negative  impacts  for the community.  The City  Council  took  no action
but directed  staff to review  options  for development  alternatives.

On January  28, 2025,  City  Council  held a workshop  to discuss  amending  requirements  for industrial
uses, improving  land  uses surrounding  future  transit  centers,  enhancing  commercial  corridors,  and
preparing  related  environmental  documentation.  Council  received  public  testimony  and discussed  the
issue.  At the conclusion,  City  Council  voted,  4-1 (Council  Member  Rios dissenting),  to direct  staff to
release  a request  for proposal  ("RFP")  to solicit  planning  and environmental  services  from  qualified
consultants  to address  the matter.  The RFP was released  to several  consulting  firms  on February  13,
2025,  and three proposals  were received.

The City's  2015 Zoning  Code prohibits  new industrial  warehouse  development  over 15,000  square
feet (SF). Through  previous  discussions,  City  Council  directed  staff to review  options  to make the city
more business  friendly  so there is a better  balance  between  businesses  and residential  neighborhoods.
Additionally,  Metro  is planning  to build  two new transit  centers  in the City  which  will  directly  affect
surrounding  properties  and potentially  be a catalyst  for improvements  in our commercial  corridors.  In
order  to foster  development  in a way  that  improves  the quality  of life  for residents,  staff  sought  a
consultant  that would  offer  the following:

 Introduction

The City is seeking  assistance  to address three  important  South Gate issues: (1) ordinance  amendment
options  regarding  industrial  uses (including  consideration  of warehouse  square footage  maximums);  (2)
land use considerations and improvements  surrounding two future  transit  centers;  and (3) enhancements
to commercial corridors to further economic development  goals.

  1.  Ordinance  Amendment:  Prepare a draft citywide  ordinance  that provides for broader or different
  considerations  for industrial  uses, particularly  in relation  to warehousing  and truck-generating
  businesses.  Critical to this issue is the City's consideration  of current  warehouse  square footage
  maximums  for individual  developments  and at what amount,  if any, future  maximums  should be
  set. Currently,  the City has a 15,000-square-foot  limit on warehousing  and part of the industria!
  land use review would  include either eliminating  or revising that limit.

  The City requires  an environmental  review to analyze potential  impacts created  by the ordinance
  and its development  standards  - most particularly  warehouse  square footage  maximums.

  2.  Future Transit  Centers:  Metro  is planning  to build two new transit  centers  in the City which will
  directly  affect surrounding  properties.  The City seeks to address  land uses surrounding  the two
  transit  sites which  are scheduled  to be constructed  over the next 10 years. The City requests
  recommendations  for the future  vision for these areas and to create overlay  zones or alternative
  land use controls  for each surrounding  area to promote  economic  benefits  for the City through
  expanded  development  zoning.  Tasks include  considering  and setting  a vision for the future  of
  these lands and providing  for the land use tools to achieve the agreed upon vision. The City will
  be partnering  with Metro  to coordinate  transit  center  planning.

  material  that has been prepared  and advise the City if the draft should be advanced  to adoption,
  modified  based on this work program,  or if the City should  pursue other alternative  actions.

  The second site is located near the 1-105 Freeway and the Green Line station  in the Hollydale  area.

  oriented  development  strategic  implementation  program  (TOD SIP). The City has been meeting

  on Garfield  Avenue  and  Paramount  Boulevard.  The  consultant  should  determine  if these
  connections  are feasible  and recommend  ways to improve  the corridors.

  commercial  corridors.  Currently  we have numerous  empty  buildings  and struggling  businesses.

as it relates  to the issues above.  Under  the direction  of the City"s Community  Development  Director,  the

consultant(s)  will provide  a range of expertise  to carry out the needs of the City. All services  provided  by

the  consultant(s)  shall  be  performed  by  individuals  who  meet  the  qualifications,  education,  and

certification/Iicensing  for the position(s). The successful consultant(s) shall also have the resources to
 provide  cost effective  and timely  services,  including  providing  outstanding  customer  service  to the City

and its related  clients.

Scope  of Services  and  Consultant's  Responsibilities

General  Expectations
The  ideal  consultant  or  consultant  team  would  work  collaboratively  with  staff  and  community
stakeholders  to  prepare  General  Plan  and  Zoning  Code  amendments  that  proactively  engage  the
community,  comply  with  all applicable  laws  and regulations,  and results  in a product  that  thoroughly
addresses  the needs of the community.  It is expected  that  the consultant  will:

  *  Research  ordinances  of other  cities to identify  applicable  requirements,  general  conditions,
  mitigation  measures,  etc. for:

  o  Industrial  uses, most  specifically  warehouse  square  footage  maximums

  o  Transit  centers/stations

  o  Major  retail/commercial  corridors

  *  Identify  constraints  and opportunities  within  the City for new warehouses  and related  square
  footage  caps, as well as other  industrial  zoning  district  amendments  the City should  consider.
  Envisioned  tasks include  providing  for a "tiered  options"  discussion  to any warehouse  square
  footage  maximums,  outlining  anticipated  impacts,  providing  a comparison  of economic  benefits,
  and recommending  mitigation  strategies  which  may be considered  by the City.

  *  Provide  defensible  strategies  for the future  recovery  of costs expended  on this work  program  by
  any future  related  development  which  may occur.

  *  Identify  streets  and intersections  that  would  be impacted  by truck  traffic  generated  from
  warehouses  and other  industrial  uses.

  *  Identify  linkages  from  industrial  areas to transit  stations/corridors  and major  commercial  areas
  and determining  ways to improve  those  linkages.

  *  Review  Metro"s  Transit  Oriented  Development  Strategic  Implementation  Program  (TOD SIP) and
  provide  recommendations  on activities  that  meet  the criteria  that  would  make the City eligible
  for funding. (https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/ba09140a9e4a476bac529c83814e3955)

  *  Provide  community  outreach  which  may include  community  meetings  to receive  resident
  feedback.  The outreach  approach  is envisioned  to leverage  similar  project  best practices,
  successes,  common  strategies  and related  code amendments  which  the Team have identified
  and to provide  for an efficient,  timely,  and expedited  approach  for the City's consideration.

  velopment  with the elimination  of physical. environmental.  and market constraints  to create a vital mix of business,
  civic,  and  pedestrian  activity.

  borhoods  or sub-markets  within  a city. EPS maintains  strong contacts with active developers  within  its key markets,

  City of Fontana

  De Novo Planning Group led the Fontana Downtown  Core Project which included changes  to the development
  code and the creation of a Development  Guide. The final work product is the Downtown  Fontana  Development
  Guide ('aGuide"),designed to be a user-friendly handbook to help guide development  in the  Downtown  Core.  De
  Novo worked with our subconsultants  to identify current market conditions  and  needed  incentives  necessary  to
  encourage  the type  of development  the City wishes  to see.

  The City identified the Downtown  Core as an area where strategically concentrated  efforts could provide  increased
  residential development  opportunities  and offer more support for mixed-uses within a focused area of the Down-
  town. Development within the Downtown  Core is implemented  through a new General Plan land use category  and
  six new  Form-Based  Code  (FBC) districts.

  The goal of this Guide is to encourage and incentivize continued economic investment in the downtown  through a
  clear process and set ofstandards  that allows for development  to respond to market conditions and reflect chang-
  ing consumption  patterns and preferences for retail. housing. and other life-style choices. This Guide provides mar-
  ket-driven opportunities for future investment and practical implementation  strategies for the continued  success
  and health of the Downtown Core. including:

  Support for housing including multi-family  housing and higher residential densities  in select  AREAS:

  Updated form-based standards and guidelines to support the areaascontinued  revitalization;

  Improved administrative  process to facilitate  by-right  project  approval  for specific  project  types;

  Development  impact  fee incentives:  and

  Top-tier environmental  clearance  that  provide  opportunities  for subsequent  projects  to tier off of the
  environmental  document  by focusing  additional  analysis  on any project-specific  impacts.
